analysis.one_liner: TVS Motor makes two-wheelers (motorcycles, scooters, mopeds) and three-wheelers, with a fast-growing electric scooter range (iQube), a large export business, a premium bet via Norton Motorcycles, and a consumer-finance arm (TVS Credit) it is now splitting off.
analysis.whats_happening: TVS Motor reported Q2 FY27 (quarter ended Sept 2026) results on 28 Oct 2026: revenue rose 44% YoY to ₹17,103 crore and standalone PAT rose 52% YoY to ₹1,377 crore (consolidated PAT, which includes the finance subsidiary, was up 46% to ₹1,219 crore). Alongside the results, the board approved a demerger of its consumer-finance business, TVS Credit, into a separate company, plus two related acquisitions to facilitate it; management expects this to take 8-10 months to complete pending regulatory approval. Volumes were strong across the board: two-wheeler EV units more than doubled (+133% YoY) and exports hit a record.
analysis.plain_terms: The headline growth numbers look spectacular, but a chunk of the YoY comparison is flattered by a GST rate cut on two-wheelers that only partly applied to last year's comparable quarter (effective 22 Sept 2025) and fully applied this time - so the 44%/52% jumps are not purely 'more bikes sold at better prices,' part of it is a base-effect quirk. Strip that out and the underlying business is still growing well (EV volumes, exports, margins all genuinely up), just not quite as dramatically as the headline suggests. The company is also in the middle of splitting off its lending arm, which will change what its balance sheet looks like once done.
analysis.quarters: Revenue and profit have accelerated through FY27: Q1 FY27 revenue was up 38% YoY with PAT up 51%; Q2 FY27 revenue was up 44% YoY with standalone PAT up 52%. EBITDA margin has edged up gradually (around 12.5% a year ago to 13.0% in Q2 FY27) rather than jumping, which is a healthier signal than the profit growth headline alone. Management flagged that the YoY comparison is distorted by the GST cut's partial effect on last year's base quarter, and said commodity cost increases (aluminium, plastics) were being partly offset by small price hikes, with no major further hikes expected in Q3/Q4. Note standalone PAT (₹1,377 crore) and consolidated PAT (₹1,219 crore, including the TVS Credit finance subsidiary) are different figures - not a contradiction, just different reporting entities.
analysis.performance_read: Returns have been exceptional on a multi-year view: the stock is up 539% over 5 years and 167% over 3 years, versus the Nifty's 29% and 21% respectively, and ahead of peer Bajaj Auto too. Over 1 year the stock is up 21% while the Nifty is actually down 11% - an unusual divergence. The stock is currently about 6% below its all-time high of ₹4,466 (hit in August 2026) and well above its 52-week low of ₹3,283. The only corporate actions on record are old stock splits (2003, 2010), already reflected in these return figures - there has been no demerger yet, so no return-series adjustment is needed at this point, though the pending TVS Credit demerger (once completed) will need to be factored into future return comparisons.
analysis.valuation_read: TVS Motor trades at roughly 52-56x trailing earnings and about 18x book value - a steep premium to peer Bajaj Auto, which trades around 25x earnings and 8x book. This premium reflects the market pricing in the EV scale-up, strong export growth, and the Norton premium-motorcycle bet, plus a higher return on equity (~34% vs Bajaj's ~29%). Whether that premium is justified is a separate question from why it exists - it requires the growth and margin trajectory seen in recent quarters to continue for several more years, and any slowdown (for instance once the GST-cut base effect fades) would make the current multiple harder to defend.
analysis.growth_read: Growth so far has been genuinely volume-led, not just margin-led: total volumes were up 27% YoY in Q2 FY27, two-wheeler EV units more than doubled, three-wheelers were up 47%, and exports were up 35% to a record. Margins have also improved, but only modestly (roughly 12.5% to 13.0% EBITDA margin over the past year) - so the combination of rising volumes and a slightly rising margin is the healthier pattern described in the company's own commentary, rather than margin expansion alone propping up profit growth. The caveat is that part of the YoY volume/revenue comparison benefits from the GST-cut base effect described above.
analysis.health_read: Profitability metrics look strong on paper (ROE ~34%, ROCE ~17-18%), but the consolidated debt-to-equity ratio of roughly 3.3x looks high mainly because it includes TVS Credit, the group's NBFC lending arm - lenders to a finance business normally carry much more debt than a manufacturer, so this number is not directly comparable to Bajaj Auto's much lower ~0.6x. A standalone, ex-financing-subsidiary debt figure was not available in this research and should be checked separately (e.g., on Screener) before drawing conclusions about the manufacturing business's own leverage. Whether operating profit is reliably converting into free cash flow was Not verified - check on Screener. The more relevant risk here looks like financial-structure complexity (the finance subsidiary, and the demerger now unwinding it) rather than core manufacturing-business risk.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (via TVS Holdings, formerly Sundaram Clayton) hold 50.27% of the company, flat for several quarters, with zero pledged shares - a clean picture on that front. Foreign institutional investors hold about 21.4% (up slightly), and domestic mutual funds hold about 15.6% (down slightly), with ICICI Mutual Fund the largest single mutual-fund holder at 6.35%. No single globally famous individual investor was identified as a disclosed holder in this research - if a well-known name is expected on this register, it does not appear to be there based on available shareholding data.
strengths: Standalone PAT up 52% YoY to ₹1,377 crore in Q2 FY27, with EBITDA margin edging up from ~12.7% to 13.0%
Two-wheeler EV volumes more than doubled YoY (186,186 units, +133%), with domestic EV penetration around 11.6% and production capacity being scaled from ~60-65,000 to ~80,000 units/month
Zero promoter share pledging against a stable 50.27% promoter stake
Record export volumes (0.539 million units, +35% YoY), broadening the business beyond the domestic market
watchpoints: Valuation is rich: ~52-56x trailing earnings and ~18x book value, roughly double Bajaj Auto's multiples on both counts
A meaningful part of the Q2 FY27 YoY growth reflects a GST-cut base effect (the comparative year-ago quarter only had ~9 days of the lower GST rate) rather than pure organic growth

Consolidated debt-to-equity of ~3.3x is inflated by the TVS Credit finance subsidiary and is not comparable to a pure manufacturer like Bajaj Auto; the pending demerger of this business (expected to take 8-10 months) will change the reported balance sheet and needs tracking through to completion
Next quarterly results date (Q3 FY27) is not yet formally confirmed by the company - sources differ between late January and mid-February 2027
analysis.one_thing: Watch for Q3 FY27 results (expected Jan-Feb 2027): with the GST-cut base effect no longer distorting the YoY comparison, this quarter will show whether volume and margin growth are holding up on their own merits, and progress on the TVS Credit demerger will start clarifying the standalone (ex-finance) balance sheet.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 revenue/PAT cross-checked across TaxGuru, Zeebiz and Business Standard; standalone (₹1,377cr) and consolidated (₹1,219cr) PAT figures both cited and distinguished. Valuation ratios (P/E, P/B, ROE) vary modestly between Screener.in and ValueResearchOnline due to pricing-date differences - ranges given rather than single points. Standalone (ex-NBFC) debt-to-equity and operating-cash-flow-to-profit conversion were Not verified - check on Screener. One FII-holding figure (5.81%) from a search snippet was discarded as an outlier in favour of two corroborating sources (~21.4%). Next-results date is unconfirmed pending a formal exchange filing.
